sourceFacts.fact: Positive skin-prick or specific-IgE tests demonstrate sensitisation.
Test positivity alone does not establish clinical allergy; interpret with exposure-related symptoms and history.
Test magnitude alone does not predict reaction severity.

layout: Four rectangular cards. Left top1 leads down to left middle2. Right middle3 is a separate history card. Cards2 and3 send two arrows converging at bottom centre4, visually combining two distinct inputs. Neutral symbols: checked result slip, labelled IgE tokens, a calendar with symptom dots, and a magnifying glass over blank paper. No patient, food icons or skin. A clear separate bottom note: A positive test alone does not prove clinical allergy. Small note: Test size does not predict reaction severity. No equals sign between sensitisation and clinical allergy.

requiredChecks: Sensitisation and symptoms are separate inputs to assessment
No implication that test positivity or test size alone diagnoses severity
No skin or diagnostic test photograph
validation.pixelChecks: Pixel review: four nodes, three arrows; positive test leads to sensitisation, and sensitisation plus a separate exposure-related symptom history converge only on assessment. Both qualifying notes are legible. Neutral tokens and documents only. Independent and clinical review pending.
